description: Issue #923 (P0): JwtOption.KnownPublicKeys exists specifically because length alone is not a sufficient weak-key test -- the developer manual's placeholder ('your-256-bit-secret-key-here-min-32-chars!') is 42 UTF-8 bytes, well past the 32-byte floor, and would pass a length-only check while still being a publicly documented value anyone can copy. This mutant neutralizes IsWeakSigningKey's blocklist check (`if (KnownPublicKeys.Contains(trimmed))` becomes `if (false && KnownPublicKeys.Contains(trimmed))`, short-circuiting to never evaluate the membership test), reintroducing exactly the length-only blind spot the blocklist exists to close. Four red tests: IsWeakSigningKey_manual_placeholder_key_returns_true_despite_being_42_bytes (the canonical case -- a >=32-byte value that ONLY the blocklist catches) and IsWeakSigningKey_well_known_default_padded_form_set_directly_returns_true (the padded 32-char form of the CLR default, also only blocklist-reachable once padded) both flip from weak to not-weak; IsWeakSigningKey_unset_key_reason_is_WeakReasonKnownPublicKey_not_TooShort and IsWeakSigningKey_demo_key_super_reason_is_WeakReasonKnownPublicKey (both <32-byte raw values that are ALSO blocklisted) do not flip to not-weak -- they still return true, but for the WRONG reason (WeakReasonTooShort instead of WeakReasonKnownPublicKey, since with the blocklist disabled they fall through to the length check instead), which the design's own Development carve-out depends on getting right (FrameworkServiceExtension.AddWtmAuthentication treats WeakReasonTooShort as strict-in-every-environment and WeakReasonKnownPublicKey as lenient-in-Development -- see the sibling mutant jwt923-devgen-environment-guard-neutralize for that guard). The green positive control (IsWeakSigningKey_31_byte_custom_key_returns_true, a non-blocklisted too-short key) proves the length check remains independently intact -- this mutant's blast radius is scoped to the blocklist path only.

'; IsWeakSigningKey_manual_placeholder_key_returns_true_despite_being_42_bytes -- 'Assert.IsTrue failed. '; IsWeakSigningKey_unset_key_reason_is_WeakReasonKnownPublicKey_not_TooShort -- 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<JwtOptions.SecurityKey is one of the publicly known placeholder values shipped with WTM.>. Actual:<JwtOptions.SecurityKey is shorter than the 32-byte (256-bit) minimum required for HMAC-SHA256 signing.>. '; IsWeakSigningKey_demo_key_super_reason_is_WeakReasonKnownPublicKey -- identical Expected/Actual shape. All four failed together in the same run (4 Failed, 26 Passed out of 30 JwtOptionTests). Confirmed via `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant jwt923-blocklist-demo-keys-neutralize`: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
